ELITE.compositionNote: No Elite Pools or Unified Portfolios allocation, rebalancing or sub-advisor change was announced as of Nov 13/26; the latest iA Clarington release found is the Oct 23/26 Active ETF distributions notice (payable Nov 10). Underlying-manager roster carried forward: PIMCO Monthly Income Fund (Canada), Mackenzie Unconstrained Fixed Income, IA Clarington Strategic Corporate Bond, BMO High Yield US Corporate Bond Index ETF, IA Clarington Loomis U.S. All Cap Growth, IA Clarington QV Global Equity, BMO MSCI EAFE Index ETF, Capital Group Global Equity (Canada). Market context for the pools: the Nov 5 tech rout (Nasdaq -5.2%, VIX ~28) and the hot Oct US CPI (Dec Fed hike ~88% priced) versus a softer Canadian labour market (6.7% unemployment, BoC hike odds ~30-35%) argue for the pools' built-in diversification and rebalancing discipline. Governance items on file remain the Mc Mahon reassignment (33 funds to iAGAM's Tej Rai/Alex Bellefleur) and the QV Canadian Small Cap PM transition (Amit Shah, effective Jul 3/26). iA Clarington AUM $26B+ (Sep 30/26). Nov 12-16 updates (condensed): Nvidia CEO exit and chip sell-offs versus a still-positive S&P week illustrated multi-manager diversification. Nov 17 update: still no Elite change announced; Monday Nasdaq -2.5% / SOX -5.3% on the Nvidia leadership vacuum plus a new US AI-chip remote-access rule, while a soft 3.1% Canadian CPI cut Dec 9 BoC hike odds to ~38% (single source) and the 10-yr eased to ~5.12% - a widening Canada-US policy gap the pools' global fixed-income managers (PIMCO, Loomis) can use. Parent iA Financial Group Q3/26: AUM/AUA $375B (+30%), individual wealth net inflows ~$1.3B. Nov 18 update: still no Elite change or November distributions notice announced; Tue Nov 17 S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53 (lowest close since July), Dow -848.75, VIX ~25.5 and software sold off (Salesforce ~-9.4%) on AI-disruption fears, while Nvidia beat after the close ($115.8B revenue, $130B Q4 guide) and USD/CAD reached ~1.43-1.435 (19-month CAD low) - an AI-winners-vs-disrupted split plus currency moves that the pools' multi-manager, multi-currency design is built to absorb. Nov 19 update: still no Elite change or November distributions notice announced; Wed Nov 18 the S&P 500 fell 0.23% to 7,323.64 (fifth straight loss, below its 200-day) while the Nasdaq rose 0.42%, Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect further hikes, USD/CAD hit ~1.434 (weakest CAD since Apr 2025), BoC Gov. Macklem announced he will step down in June 2027, and Anthropic priced a record ~$81.3B IPO at $83 - rates, currency and AI-concentration crosscurrents the pools' multi-manager, multi-currency design (PIMCO, Loomis, iAGAM) is built to absorb. Nov 20 update: still no Elite change or November distributions notice announced (the Nov 2025 notice came Nov 21, so one is likely within days); Thu Nov 19 the S&P 500 fell ~2.0% to 7,175.83 (sixth straight loss, -5.1% week-to-date), the Dow closed below 50,000 for the first time since June, VIX rose to ~28.4, Anthropic's debut closed +17% at $97.17 after opening ~$111.50, NVDA hit a 52-week low ($145.98) and USD/CAD held ~1.433 - a broad risk-off week the pools' rebalancing and multi-manager fixed income are designed to cushion. Nov 21 update: still no Elite change or November distributions notice indexed; Fri Nov 20 the S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6,910.39 and entered a correction (with the Dow), the Nasdaq lost 5.28% and turned negative for 2026, NVDA fell 14% on a reported SEC accounting probe, VIX closed 35.89 (~40 intraday), and the US 10-yr fell back to ~4.97% - stocks down, bonds up, which is exactly the offset the pools' multi-manager fixed income (PIMCO, Loomis) and rebalancing discipline are built to deliver. Nov 23 update: still no Elite change or November distributions notice indexed; Mon Nov 23 Asia followed Friday's correction (Kospi -5.8%, Hang Seng -1.8%, Tokyo closed), with PCE Wed and Thanksgiving Thu - global, multi-manager diversification remains the core conversation. Nov 24 update: still no Elite change or November distributions notice indexed; Mon Nov 23 the S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq 6.51% (best day since Apr 2025) after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, with VIX easing to ~26.6 - a Friday-correction / Monday-rebound pair that illustrates the cost of exiting and the value of the pools' disciplined, multi-manager rebalancing. Nov 25 update: still no Elite change or November distributions notice indexed; Tue Nov 24 the Dow closed above 50,000 for the first time while the Nasdaq fell 1.48% and NVDA 5.9% - another rotation day that favours diversified, rebalanced multi-manager portfolios.
